---
title: Cases, hospitalizations, and deaths, fitted to data
jupyter: python3
---

Data on an epidemic is rarely the number infected: it is reported cases, hospital admissions, or deaths, each a share of infections, some time after infection. In Starsim these are outcomes: results computed from the model's flows, with a share, a delay, and (for a stay in hospital) a duration, that don't change the epidemic itself. This page adds three outcomes to an SIR, makes weekly data from the model with a known β, and fits β to it.

## The model

| Parameter | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| β | fitted, between 0.05 and 1 per day | Rate of infection; the data was made with 0.25 |
| Infectious period | 10 days | Mean time in I (exponential) |
| Cases | 50% of infections, 5 days later | Reported cases |
| Hospitalizations | 5% of infections, 7 days later, for 10 days | People in hospital |
| Deaths | 20% of those hospitalized, about 14 days later | Lognormal delay (mean 14 days, standard deviation 5) |
| Population | 1,000,000 | |
| Infectious at the start | 0.1% | |

```{python}
import starsim as ss
ss.options(jupyter=True)

beta = ss.par(0.3, bounds=[0.05, 1.0]) # A parameter to fit, with its starting value and bounds
S, I, R = ss.states('S I R')
infection = S >> I @ beta*I
recovery  = I >> R @ ss.days(10)
cases     = ss.outcome(0.5*infection, delay=ss.days(5))
hosp      = ss.outcome(0.05*infection, delay=ss.days(7), duration=ss.days(10))
deaths    = ss.outcome(0.2*hosp, delay=ss.lognorm_ex(mean=14, std=5, unit='days'))
sir = ss.Disease(infection, recovery, cases, hosp, deaths, init=dict(I=0.001), name='sir')

pars = dict(total_pop=1e6, start='2020-01-01', stop='2020-06-01')
```

The outcomes are not states, so the diagram, from `diagram()`, is an SIR's:

```{python}
sir.diagram()
```

## Data

The data is made from the model itself, with β = 0.25, as weekly counts of cases and deaths with Poisson noise, as in real reporting. Since the right answer is known, this checks that the fit can find it.

```{python}
truth = ss.Sim(sir, pars=dict(beta=0.25), rand_seed=2, verbose=0, **pars)
truth.run()
data = truth.to_data(['cases', 'deaths'], resample='week')
data.head()
```

## Result

The data is matched to results by name (`cases` and `deaths`), and each week of data is compared with the model's total over that week. `sim.fit()` fits every parameter with bounds to every result with data:

```{python}
sim = ss.Sim(sir, data=data, **pars)
fit = sim.fit()
fit.plot()
```

```{python}
fit.pars
```

β comes out at 0.25, the value the data was made with.
